name: ws-transport-faults
description: Journey #14's transport half (docs/RELIABILITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §5 item 14, §9 "WS transport" row; task D2): the same linear pipeline as journey #1, run through a `WsFaultProxy` (`faults/net-proxy.ts`) in front of the hermetic e2e-server, once per ws-* fault. `ws-delay`/`ws-fragment` still complete normally (added latency / smaller TCP writes never corrupt a length-prefixed WS frame stream) and pass every declared invariant with a real terminal `job_update` observed. `ws-drop-no-fin`/`ws-stall-reads`/`ws-abrupt-close` black-hole the client's socket by design — this driver's client legitimately never observes a terminal `job_update` (the ws-server driver's own timeout race, not a hang, ends the run `"timeout"`) — `reliability/harness/tests/journeys/ws-transport-faults.test.ts` asserts that terminal-uniqueness is *expected* to report `terminal-uniqueness.missing` for those three (a faithful client-side symptom, not server corruption) and, separately, that the server itself stayed healthy: a fresh unfaulted connection can still run this same workflow to completion afterward. `lifecycle-pairing`/`cleanup-leaks` are declared here because both explicitly tolerate a sparse/absent record (see their module docs) — `terminal-uniqueness` is deliberately left off this journey's declared matrix and asserted per-fault by the dedicated test instead, since it legitimately (and correctly) fires for the three black-hole faults. `timeoutMs` is the completion budget for `ws-delay`/`ws-fragment` and is the same 30s every other pipeline journey declares; the three black-hole faults are waiting for a frame that never arrives, so the test shortens the budget for those rather than making every run pay a number picked for dead time.
